reason: The text emphasizes hierarchy throughout multiple dimensions: (1) Divine hierarchy—God's supreme authority is repeatedly asserted through direct commands to Jonah ('וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ יוֹנָ֥ה'), God's control of nature, and Jonah's ultimate submission to God's will; (2) Prophetic authority—Jonah is positioned as God's authoritative messenger to Nineveh, whose proclamation prompts mass repentance; (3) Political hierarchy—The king of Nineveh and his nobles ('מֶ֣לֶך נִֽינְוֵ֔ה' and 'גְדֹלָ֖יו') issue binding decrees that command the entire population and animals to fast and repent ('מִטַּ֧עַם הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וּגְדֹלָ֖יו'); (4) Institutional obedience—Obedience to authority figures (God, the prophet, the king) is presented as the appropriate and morally correct response. The narrative structure itself privileges hierarchical relationships as essential to its plot and resolution.
